Hot Wheels RC Car, Remote-Control 2017 Nissan GT-R in 1:64 Scale, Works On and Off Hot Wheels Track, Includes Track Adapter​​​​ I got two of these Hot Wheels remote control cars - the Hot Wheels R/C 1:64 Scale 2017 Nissan Gt-R and the Rodger Dodger. First off, I have to say that they are lots of fun.

They run on the floor well, but they also fit our Hot Wheels track, giving a variety of interesting options - but I preferred the floor as you have freeform options you won't have on the track. As an example, if you want to turn around dramatically, just turn with the remote without going forward or back. But they're a blast when you run one on the track, as well! They're faster than I thought they'd be, and while it took a few minutes to get used to the steering on the remote, after that they were responsive and easy to control. I let my husband drive the Gt-R so we could race, and he also had a learning curve with the steering and then found the car to be a blast.

I like the way the remotes bind without a hassle, and you can control either car with either remote, but it won't control both simultaneously, so no problem for racing.

I really like these cars, although I think the 2017 Nissan Gt-R is more attractive, but that's a personal taste thing. Both cars are fun, run well, and you can do a few tricks with them. They run well on our hardwood floors and can be raced using Hot Wheels track, as well. I think one of these cars would make a good gift for older kids as well as anyone into Hot Wheels.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels RC Car, Remote-Control 2017 Nissan GT-R in 1:64 Scale, Works On and Off Hot Wheels Track, Includes Track Adapter​​​​

Putting the chickens in the nest, collecting the eggs into the bucket, moving Barbie around and having conversations with the chickens, making the chickens say peep peep peep!

My complaints about this Barbie doll are my usual complaints, I wish that this Barbie was shaped a little bit more like Daisy, and I wish that this Barbie moved a little bit more like the sports Barbies. I wish that all Barbies off the shelf would come with more functional joints so that Barbie could do more interesting things. However! My three-year-old has noticed no lack, and I think the fact that Barbie is rather inflexible makes her somewhat easier to get dressed, which is fun. Mattel Disney Princess Royal Castle Disney Princess Royal Castle is a cute castle that is sure to be a hit with young princesses everywhere who are addicted to the Disney Princesses and love anything associated with them. This castle is much like other Disney castles available on the market, with a few added accessories and everything a young girl needs to enjoy hours of imaginative play.

I have two girls who have been Disney fanatics since a young age and still love anything related to Disney- especially the princesses. Their love of Belle, Snow White, Sleeping Beauty, Aerial, and the other princesses was reason enough to bring this toy into the house. Taking it from the box and assembling a few items was all it took to get the castle ready for play. In no time at all, they were running upstairs to find all of their Disney Princess dolls and bringing then downstairs to play with their new castle.

Disney Princess Royal Castle is a cute castle and very girly in appearance, making it just right for Disney Princess fans. My girls like the castle and they love anything that accommodates their Disney princess dolls. They also like making up stories as they play, but they and I both agree that this castle isn't they greatest one with which they have played. One reason is the lack of any sound effects, movements, etc. I am thankful that the castle includes no lights or anything that requires batteries, but it would be nice if it at least offered some mechanical movements, sound chips, or something else. Another issue is the small upper level. This is where the bedroom is located and it is much smaller than the area below. It would be better if the two levels were a little more even.

My girls love anything Disney Princess related and they like this castle, but they do not rank it among their favorites and it is easy to see why. The lack of at least a simple sound effect, the small number of accessories, and the lack of folding or another way to make storing easier all add up to an average toy overall.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Disney Princess Royal Castle

Snap Circuits Snaptricity, Electronics Exploration Kit (Stem Building), For Kids 8+ Initially I bought Snap-Circuits for my 4 and 5 year old boys. I found the collection of capacitors, resistors, integrated circuit modules, and transistors was a little too abstract, and I was thinking I really wanted more stuff like electro-magnets, relays, motors, generators, switches, potentiometers, and maybe resistive loads like light bulbs and diodes -- more basic electrical stuff, of which there's some in the circuit kits but not a lot.

My boys are 5 and 6 now. I added Snaptricity to our collection of mostly unexplored Snap-Circuits, and suddenly they're creating all kinds of basic circuits with switches, buttons, lights, motors, and electro-magnets. They're starting to understand the flow of electricity, polarity, magnetism, and resistance (as they add more loads to their circuits). I've set the transistors and stuff aside for now, because there's tons of stuff to do with these more basic components first. For older children, they might be ready for the electronic components sooner, but with my younger kids, these electrical parts are great.

We do not follow the instructions. So it helps to have extra components on hand instead of the minimum number required for the book experiments. Some of our circuits are more than elegant and minimalist. I recommend buying two kits, or this kit and another one like the 100 or 300.

The brilliant thing about these components is the incredibly simple and effective button snap-connectors. The only downside to these components is they are encased in plastic for durability. The plastic is clear so the internal components can be seen. This is really a good thing, but it's worthwhile to have a coil/electromagnet that is un-encased, as well as a speaker/microphone (electromagnet with a diaphragm) that is not encased, and a motor that can be disassembled/dissected.
text_fidelity_b: Snap Circuits Snaptricity, Electronics Exploration Kit (Stem Building), For Kids 8+

text_fidelity_a:
TAG -- Live-Action Elimination Competition -- Eliminate Your Target Until You're The Last One Standing -- 4-10 Players -- Ages 14+ When I was in high school my senior class played an elimination game that was vaguely similar to this (and has been around for years and is still played across the country). Each person drew a name and that was the "target", and there were only loose rules on how to "eliminate" your target (most memorable weapon was a seltzer bottle), and graduation was the time limit. TAG is basically a formalization of that game, with fewer players and more specifics on elimination.

My graduating class had over 500 people, and not all of them played the game. Still, with 50+ players and months to play, it was unwieldy then. TAG limits the game to 10 players max, and the time frame can span anywhere from an hour or two to several weeks. Though the rules are flexible enough to allow for playing for months, this gets a bit cumbersome when having a small player pool.

Each player gets an ID card ("credentials") and a target name. Unlike the more informal version of the game, players are given specific instructions on how to eliminate their target. It might be luring the target to a location or lying in wait, getting the target to do something, or more. Nailing the target with the squirt gun or "poisoning" their food with salt might be fun but if it's not on the specific method card, it doesn't count. Once you've eliminated your target, your next target becomes whoever your original target was stalking. Gameplay continues until there's only one player left.

I like the way this game refines the elimination process, and I like the smaller, more limited scope. This makes it a good game for family events, fun in the dorms at school or even a company morale booster.

If you've ever played the old elimination game, this will be familiar territory. If you haven't it's a fun introduction. There's reasonably good replayability and there's enough flexibility to either play quickly or draw it out for days and weeks.
text_fidelity_b: TAG -- Live-Action Elimination Competition -- Eliminate Your Target Until You're The Last One Standing -- 4-10 Players -- Ages 14+

Wonder Wheels by Battat – Dump Truck, Tow Truck, Cement Truck – Toy Truck Combo Set for Toddlers Age 1 & Up (3 Pc) – 100% Recyclable , Yellow This is a mixed bag. The dump truck is GREAT! Much better than the green toys version because the dump part goes all the way vertical to dump out. YAY!!! My 5 year old was all over this, mixing all manner of unappetizing mud pies, twig sandwiches and grass clumps and moving the muck from one place to another.

The cement mixer is AWFUL. It is infuriating that they make a cement mixer with no opening to put stuff! It has this tiny little grate that lets out small amounts of dry sand or very teeny tiny pebbles. I guess you are supposed to cram it in through the tiny grate that is supposed to let stuff out? God forbid you get dirt in there and water, and it clumps up, as has happened with many other trucks in a similar vein. I had no issue turning the drum smoothly and appreciate that the drum can be angled downward to dump out, but this was pretty much the most disappointing disaster of a cement mixer I could imagine given there is no mechanism for getting stuff IN, or cleaning it. Who DOES that? That designer or committee needs to be fired.

The tow truck is mixed. I love the pull out ramp. It sticks a bit and is a little harder to use than desired, but overall good. But the hook part and the bar do not function well. The hook is stuck onto this boxy bar so it is hard to actually get it to hook to a vehicle, not impossible, but could have been done better. You can pull the bar out an inch and a half but then trying to push it back in, I injured myself/ hurt my finger. I am a grownup, so it is hard to imagine that this was truly vetted for use by toddlers if it needs that much force. Then the angling mechanism also requires a lot of oomph. My five year old can do it but finds it frustrating. 2 year old cannot.

Overall the packaging of having this set of three harmonizing full size trucks is great. Would be fun to pull out when guests come to loosen everyone up together and give everyone something to play with. But the design flaws make it hard to truly recommend. In a dry, clean sandbox, this would probably be most successful since the cement mixer would actually function.
text_fidelity_b: Wonder Wheels by Battat – Dump Truck, Tow Truck, Cement Truck – Toy Truck Combo Set for Toddlers Age 1 & Up (3 Pc) – 100% Recyclable , Yellow

LEGO Speed Champions Formula E Panasonic Jaguar Racing Gen2 car and Jaguar I-PACE eTROPHY 76898 Building Kit (564 Pieces),Multicolor,Standard I really like these new redesigned speed champions models that are 8 studs wide. The previous generation was 6 studs wide and while that worked great for a few car shapes, many of the models just looked weird in my opinion because the length was out of proportion to the width.

With the new wider chassis design there is a lot more room for the designers to keep the proportions more realistic and also add lots more detail to the models. My only complaint is that they are still using the same size wheel/tire molds from the previous generation which means the wheels are now out of proportion to the larger chassis.. It doesn't look too bad though and I still think its a big improvement over the previous generation. Hopefully next year they will come out with new molds for the wheel area to make them even better.

This set offers a fun build with a lot of neat pieces and advanced building techniques.. and the price per piece of only 6.2 cents for a licensed set is pretty great! Its pretty rare to find larger sets significantly under 10cents per piece, so this one offers a pretty good value compared to most others even at full MSRP. Definitely recommended for any LEGO fan.

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball Unlike traditional jigsaw puzzles, the pieces are made of hard plastic rather than cardboard or foam, which means it's more durable. I remember growing up with jigsaw puzzles where the pictures got chipped because the paper would peel off the cardboard. The colors are bright, shiny and very decorative. Also unlike cardboard jigsaws, the pieces actually stay together and the ball can be held up when finished. Very cool.

On the negative side, I don't like the fact that the pieces are numbered on the back. For me, this takes away the challenge of being detail-oriented and noticing the tiny details that make one piece go with another. It feels like a dumbing-down to me. I could see the numbered sequence being good for younger kids, but not for something that's geared to 10 and older.

Other than that, this is a high quality, solidly made puzzle that families would enjoy doing together.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball

Mega Construx Pokemon Power Pack Kadabra Construction Set with Character Figures, Building Toys for Kids, 6 years and up (92 Pieces) The Mega Construx Kadabra is better suited for display rather than actual play. His hands fall off quite easily. The play feature of the purple orb is pretty meh. But due to his ball and socket joints, he stands without needing assistance or to lean against anything.

Assembly takes about 30 minutes. The instructions are clear; the hardest part is often clicking the pieces together. My fingers actually hurt after I was finished, due to the pressure I needed to exert to get some of the pieces to fit together. I’ve noticed this with other Mega Construx sets. I wish they would fix this, as it makes it harder for young kids to do this on their own.

The set is rated 6+, which I would say is accurate for the instructions and building. The main difficulty will be snapping pieces together. I had imprints on my fingers -- that’s how hard it can be to get some pieces to fit. Which is ironic, considering how easily some other pieces, like Kadabra’s hands, fall off the finished Pokémon.

The printing on his face and chest is a lighter pink than it appears on the box.

The moustache fur is made of a floppy plastic, so it does move around when the figure is moved. This was probably my favorite part of the set, as I thought it added character to the Kadabra. A little piece of advice: I recommend fitting the moustache around the knob of the piece meant to secure it, putting it together upside down instead of the way the instructions show. This way you can ensure it’s evenly lined up.

hand2mind Science Kit Music Maker, STEM Activities for Kids Ages 5-7, STEM Toys, Kids Storybook, Pan Flute, Ocean Drum, and Box Guitar, 10 at Home Science Experiments for Kids We are having fun doing the exercises in this hand2mind Science Kit Music Maker, DIY Kits For Kids Ages 5-7. I would say the age range can be up to age 9 actually. Everything you need to make three instruments is in the kit with instructions on how to make 4. The water xylophone doesn't have any materials to make it, so you'll need your own same sized glass jars/cups and food coloring to do that exercise. I wish the explanations were a bit more simplistic for 5-6 years olds. I feel like this is better geared toward older kids 7-9 to understand the science behind sound. My almost 8-year-old kind of got it, but not really.

In the kit, there's a book that has a story. The beginning of the story doesn't really make sense or tie in at all to the ultimate situation at hand. However, the gist eventually becomes a classroom of kids with their music teacher making instruments for a performance. Once he walks you through the 4 different instruments (only three have materials to make an instrument) then you'll start building your instrument and experimenting with them. I feel like the materials are ok sturdy; however, I have instructed my son to not play with them unless we are doing the experiments (until we are finished with all of them). Simply because I do not want them to become damaged before we get to finish. So far we have completed the box guitar, which was easy enough. We did it together with me mainly explaining the instructions and my son completing the tasks. The only thing I had to help with was folding the box. After that, we went through 3 of the 4 experiments. We'll complete the 4th experiment and then move on to the next instrument at a later date. With COVID, it's been nice and important to stretch science kits like this one out over multiple days. I'm glad I saved this for a rainy day because now we've had something nice and fun to do all while responsibly quarantining.
text_fidelity_b: hand2mind Science Kit Music Maker, STEM Activities for Kids Ages 5-7, STEM Toys, Kids Storybook, Pan Flute, Ocean Drum, and Box Guitar, 10 at Home Science Experiments for Kids

2021 Smart Watches for Women, Fitness Tracker with Blood Pressure Heart Rate Blood Oxygen Monitor, IP68 Waterproof Activity Tracker with Pedometer, Smartwatch for Android Phones I've been on the search for a smartwatch that meets all my needs. I'd like to find one that has a small watch face, bands that can be changed, uses a good app, and can monitor O2, sleep, and a wide variety of exercise. This watch was a perfect 10 in looking nice for my small wrists, and bands that can be changed. Unfortunately it fell quite short of the mark for everything else I needed.

The app has me ready to put this watch back in the box and try something else. It's a really clunky app compared to others I've tried (Fitbit, Da Fit). The exercise feature is very limiting and doesn't account for any indoor exercise like a stationary bike, aerobics, treadmill, etc. Most of the time the steps on the app are wrong compared to the steps on the watch, even after trying to sync it again. It's disappointing that there's so few watch faces to choose from. I can't even choose the screen analog look watch face that is displayed on the box, it's not an option on the app at all. The O2 feature is nice, and so is the sleep feature. I do hope they'll continue to work on the app, it does have potential but doesn't work well for me as it is right now.

I'm also having some trouble trying to use the long press on the watch itself to select features. It's just not working no matter how often I try. It's really disappointing that such a beautiful watch has so many problems. I would have really liked to use it as my main watch, but my search will have to continue on.
text_fidelity_b: 2021 Smart Watches for Women, Fitness Tracker with Blood Pressure Heart Rate Blood Oxygen Monitor, IP68 Waterproof Activity Tracker with Pedometer, Smartwatch for Android Phones

Diamond Painting Stickers Kits for Kids, Paint by Numbers Diamonds for Adult Beginners,DIY 5D Diamond Art Mosaic Stickers I have the “28PCS POKEMON” option in this pack of diamond painting stickers from BLYNN. This option is really a multipack of different themes: Pokemon (12 stickers), Star Wars (8 stickers), and Princesses (8 stickers).

This is a great way to try diamond painting since the images are small. They vary in size, but are roughly 3 inches by 3 inches. An image this size takes about 30 minutes for a beginner. When you are finished putting the diamond drills on the image, you can peel off the back and it’s a sticker.

The pack includes two toolkits, so you can have two kids working on their chosen sticker at the same time. The diamond paintings can be cut apart -- I recommend an adult do this part, since the edges are close together -- and then worked on separately. That way you don’t have to remove the protective plastic from the whole sheet.

The pack also includes the drills for every sticker. Some of the colors are really off. Snorlax should be dark teal, but the drills are dark green. Eevee should be brown, but the drills are yellow-orange. The drills come in tear-open plastic baggies; I recommend having some small resealable baggies or containers ready if you aren’t going to do all of the stickers at once, since they often share colors (like yellow-orange for Eevee and Charmander).
text_fidelity_b: Diamond Painting Stickers Kits for Kids, Paint by Numbers Diamonds for Adult Beginners,DIY 5D Diamond Art Mosaic Stickers

Kinetic Sand, Bake Shoppe Playset with 1lb of Kinetic Sand and 16 Tools and Molds, for Ages 3 and up I have mixed feelings about this set because my kids absolutely loved playing with the kinetic sand. The bakeshop playset idea was fun, and while the small number of creative tools made it so that my children were asking for their Play-Doh tools to go with it almost immediately, the new texture was so much fun for them that I cannot give this a poor review. I also loved that we had a miniature Barbie Chelsea sandbox with some sandbox toys, and this kinetic sand filled the sandbox perfectly and allowed us to play at making little sandbox molds, scooping the sand, and incorporating the Chelsea doll into play. That set had previously come with the teeny tiny little container of a kinetic sand like material, but having an ample amount was really fun.

However, we discovered the problem with this stuff about 1/2 hour after cleaning up. I walked past the hard floor area where we had cleaned up afterwards, and nearly fell on my butt. I had already, I thought, cleaned up all the pieces of clay on the floor and given one or two areas a quick wipe down with cleaner, so I was puzzled as to why the floor was so slippery. I cleaned the floor there, and walked around and forgot about it for about five more minutes, when I walked by and almost fell on my butt in another spot. Then my husband almost fell. Then my child did fall. I cleaned the floor thoroughly and there were still patches of occasional area that were just ridiculously slippery, and I don't really understand how it withstood numerous attacks with normal household cleaners. But for days we were discovering slippery areas on our floor that made it really not safe.

So I would give the caveat that if you are going to allow your children to play with kinetic sand, do so outside so that you do not end up with a dangerous situation on your own hard floors.

Monster High Travel Scaris Scooter Vehicle Monster High toys and accessories are a huge hit with their fan base and the Travel Scaris Convertible vehicle is bound to be a big hit with kids who love Monster High. It is a stylish and attractive toy vehicle with a design that sets it apart from the average kid's toy vehicle.

I'm not usually very impressed with toy vehicles because I have seen so many of them and because most of them look very similar. But this toy vehicle grabbed my attention. The cool, eye- catching, all- around design pattern is one that is bound to warrant a second look and both adults and kids alike will find that it easily stands out against other toy vehicles.

Aside from the exterior, this Monster High vehicle does have other features that make it cool. The stylish wheels glide smoothly across a tile floor or a table without any problem and the vehicle seats up to four Monster High dolls. Rather than have all four dolls face forward, this convertible is a two- seat model with a pair of seats that are actually on top of the trunk, where the dolls face backward. Again, it's something unique that you don't find with other toy vehicles.

The Monster High Travel Scaris Vehicle doesn't have any lights or sounds. This may bother some youngsters, but it is better from an adult perspective because it means no batteries to buy and more imagination required. Most kids will not mind anyway- they will find the vehicle so cool and fun that they will not even notice that it doesn't make noise or have any lights. And another advantage is that boys and girls both seem to like this toy. Girls like it because its Monster High and boys like it because, well, it's a vehicle, which is a toy normally associated with boys.

This Monster High vehicle doesn't have opening side doors, and this is one quality that I wish was different because it would not only look cool, but it would also make it easier to place the dolls into the seats. But other than that, this is a fun, nice- looking toy that belongs in the home of every Monster High fan.

Winning Moves Games Classic Twister Ah, the memories I have from playing Twister when I was 16 and drove a red Firebird. Paul, who I wished was my boyfriend was interested in me only as a friend, so the best way I had to get close to him was to invite friends over for a game of Twister. Memories are interesting because I recall exactly what he and I were both wearing -- he in a light blue oxford Gant shirt and me in my self designed and sewn striped wide legged hip-hugger slacks, solid shirt and matching striped vest. I can't tell you who else was there, but we had a full house and we had a blast with my little sister calling our moves and tattling when we were having TOO much fun.

[[ASIN:B00HVTH2MC Classic Twister]] can be played by most ages, provided the bodies are somewhat agile and the individuals are not really shy. The vinyl mat allows for between 2 and 4 people, no more. A game lasts less than 15 minutes usually with the winner being the person who remains on the mat without falling over. A designated person who is not on the mat spins the little plastic on cardboard wheel and those playing place the appropriate limb on a designated spot. For color blind people, your friends will let you know where to put that foot or hand, I guarantee. It is a really fun physical game that stimulates conversation and breaks the ice. I noticed that there are several versions of the game available as of today but cannot tell you what the differences are or why the prices vary. What I can tell you is that this is a really amusing game for all ages, even those who can't actually do the moving but can participate from the peanut gallery.

text_fidelity_a:
Drone Home -- First Ever Game With a Real, Flying Drone -- Great, Family Fun! -- For 2-4 Players -- Ages 8+ I have very mixed feelings about this game. First, it is REALLY FUN, and my kids and I were laughing really hard playing it. The drone taking off is really a lot of fun and cool to see, and even our little 3 year old who is too young to play was enamored by it and shrieking when it would lift off with little playing pieces inside! Really a lot of fun.
That being said, there are 3 caveats to be aware of:
1)I don't feel comfortable letting the kids play this alone. The drone comes crashing down sometimes and I want an adult or kid old enough to be able to catch it to avoid hurting anyone / furniture, or crashing so hard it cracks the plastic (a part of the drone siding already popped out, but I was able to push it back into place).

2) I feel like this game won't last very long. The pieces are VERY easily lost, as they end up being flung around the room as you play. Also, the drone lifting off bumps into the ceiling easily (thankfully we have cathedral ceilings in our living and had to move the game over to there, otherwise it would hit and come crashing down fast). It's only a matter of time before the plastic breaks or pieces get lost forever.

3) I dove to catch it on the way down after a particular round, and it hurt my finger. Nothing major, didn't hurt more than stubbing your toe on furniture or stepping on a lego- it has a safety to shut the propeller if it detects something in the way, but I was still surprised. I was fine, but one of my kids would have been crying if it happened to them.

My daughter actually suggested we try playing it outside next time, which might solve some of the issues- can't do damage to the house and everyone can duck for cover until it crashes into the grass. Wind might make it less fun though. HOWEVER- this was a TON OF FUN TO PLAY, so even with all those caveats, and even considering it might not last more than a few months in my household, I'd still consider it worth playing even for those few times. The look on their faces when the drone takes off is PRICELESS, and worth it even if you only get to play it once.
text_fidelity_b: Drone Home -- First Ever Game With a Real, Flying Drone -- Great, Family Fun! -- For 2-4 Players -- Ages 8+

Pass the Stache Board Game This is definitely not a cerebral or strategizing game. It is pure reaction, action, and laughter. We played a number of rounds as a way to break the ice between to families of children who had not met yet, and it was perfect. The rules are as simple as you can get, flip a card up, if it matches the color or shape of your mustache, hit it with your suction cupped mustache and claim the card. It you suction cup up one that doesn't match, you pay a two card penalty and he who ends with the most cards wins. Ok there are a couple more rules, but that is the gyst. There are also an all smash card and a none smash cards. But seriously, that is the rules right there.

The mustaches themselves are great. They are a blast in themselves as our kids giggled continually at the look of the mustaches touch to everyone's upper lip. They are made strong with decent suction cups below them. It is fairly easy to strike a card and pull it up with the suction cup. And the cards are well made to take the abuse.

As for game play, the rounds are short and exciting. Some feelings got hurt, but for the most part it was an uproarious game which put smiles on everyone's face. Scoring is easy...just count up the cards you won. Personally, I don't think this will be a classic game, but it willl be pulled out in our house many times.

Kinetic Sand, Bake Shoppe Playset with 1lb of Kinetic Sand and 16 Tools and Molds, for Ages 3 and up Kinetic sand is a fun activity for young kids, like regular sand it has tendency to get all over the place if not contained in a tray or plastic dish but it is easy to clean up and unlike play-doh and other similar modeling toys it doesn't ever dry out. This bake shop set comes with a roller and variety of stamps and molds to make cookies and cupcakes which are all nice quality. I especially like that the molds can fit within the roller for easy storage.

The only downside to this set is that kinetic sand is not really ideal for molding since it has a tendency to flow and collapse if not packed very tightly. Our 5 year old was trying to reproduce some of the cupcake designs shown on the box and was getting frustrated because the sand kept falling apart when she added the icing on top of the cupcake base. I tried to do it myself and was able to reproduce the design but it required packing the sand very tightly and then being very delicate when removing from the molds..

We like kinetic sand, and we like the molds that come with this set but we will probably use them primarily with play-doh instead of kinetic sand because these small molds are kind of difficult for kids to use with kinetic sand. We have some other larger ice cream molds that we have used with kinetic sand in the past, they are easier to use because they are smoother and release the sand without requiring such a delicate touch to prevent it crumbling.
text_fidelity_b: Kinetic Sand, Bake Shoppe Playset with 1lb of Kinetic Sand and 16 Tools and Molds, for Ages 3 and up

text_fidelity_a:
Klutz Bath and Body Activity Kit Multicolor, 9" Length x 1.75" Width x 9" Height When it comes to making things on our own, my household is a busy place with lots of creativity flowing. When we saw this kit, we could not wait to use it. Finally after waiting due to issues in our house which required a lot of remodeling, we were able to try this out. Let's see how it was..

WHAT IS THIS KIT LIKE?
This kit is one of our favorites. Being those who love color, we enjoyed the beautiful colored box. The box has a very detailed booklet on it which outlines every single project in the box and tells how to do the project. The photography is perfect and easy to read and follow. The layout and writing is perfect for using with children- both younger and older. There is not only an assortment of ingredients all carefully labeled and packaged, but there are little boxes and other decorative containers that you put together to give or display your creations in. I love that the bags are also labeled with what project it is good for and the page number in the booklet which is part of the box, so you won't lose it.

HOW DID OUR CREATIONS TURN OUT?
We had such fun with this. We enjoyed making the Bubble Bath Bon Bons most of all, and they really did work nicely in the tub. We have not done ALL of the projects yet, but the Bon Bons are the favorite so far- especially the marble method of mixing the colors. The little boxes that you put together are really cute and perfect to give as gifts. We also had fun with the lip mask.

ANY DRAWBACKS?
You will have to buy some fresh ingredients for this kit. That means that your treatments will be natural and safe for the face as well as fresh. Strawberry, lemon, avocado, banana, milk, honey, coconut milk, fine sugar or colored sugar, yogurt, and olive oil. Be prepared to have those on hand if you want to do the entire kit. We didn't mind though as we use these things in our home anyway, except for sugar, but I did have some on hand from a sugar scrub we experimented with in the past.

THE BOTTOM LINE
With all of the more unusual ingredients supplied, this kit is great fun to do. My daughter and I had a wonderful time with it. The colors, layout, and packaging are top notch. With the exception of having to provide quite a few fresh ingredients, this is easy and convenient but great fun when you finally do get to have your SPA day!

MY RATING
FIVE STARS! This can be used from young kids who are able to do this with supervision up to older kids- even late teens- who really want to have fun creating a spa day. I can also see using the principles used in this in the future creating a spa day for grandma or others that the kids want to reach out to for a special day.
text_fidelity_b: Klutz Bath and Body Activity Kit Multicolor, 9" Length x 1.75" Width x 9" Height

4. Though the arms rotate around the sun, the individual planets do not rotate. So to explain night and day to your child, you'll need to manually rotate Earth. 3 stars.

Melissa & Doug Victorian Wooden Dollhouse Furniture This is a beautiful set, with the vast majority of the pieces being thoughtfully designed and thoughtfully put together. I like that each of the room sets goes together really well, so that you have a cohesive feel throughout your dollhouse without everything feeling identical.

The quality level on some of this is absolutely stunning given that it is at a reasonable price point and made for children. I really love some of the pullout drawers that are actually functional, and the upholstery on the bed and couch, chairs and Ottoman are incredible. I think my favorite piece might be the show off cabinet that has clear plastic windows, so that you can display things in the dollhouse. We have some miniature flower vases and things like that that fit perfectly.

There were a few things that came with the quality a little bit off. The toilet arrived broken, and not only was it broken, but I could tell that the way it was put together facilitated it arriving broken. The toilet seat pins were attached in a way that the toilet seat cannot close properly over the main body of the toilet, and the part that broke off, the back toilet tank, showed very cheap pressboard material underneath, which I did not expect from Melissa and Doug brand. There were a few doors, like the refrigerator, that were also put on a little bit diagonally in a way that would drive type a grown-up a bit crazy.

The vast majority of the things however appeared to be made of real wood and had a really incredible quality and design. I put them into a new dollhouse that I'm creating for fun to play with with my kids, and it's been really fun to accessorize and make everything fit into the dollhouse in a way that feels truly special.

The packaging is ready to be dressed up or wrapped as a gift. The packaging I got was a big, wide, flat cardboard box with a plain brown exterior that you lift the lid and find a bunch of brown paper wrapped furniture. If you wrapped this with wrapping paper, it would be perfect as a gift, but if given right out the box, it definitely lacks a little sparkle. That said, once anybody realizes what is inside, the excitement level of unwrapping each individual piece was kind of like Easter, or Christmas. Really incredible.

Overall I'm really pleased with this set, and so many of these special pieces seem heirloom quality and like things that we will be so happy to continue playing with or keep for grandchildren someday.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Victorian Wooden Dollhouse Furniture

text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer Ultimate EZ Folding Wagon for kids and cargo, Red, Model Number: 3900 The foldable flyer is so far so good--easily put together, nicely constructed, easily foldable and relatively compact.

Packaging: It comes in a large box already folded. Separate parts are minimal: the canopy (folded), the handle, two wheels packed separately with their screws, the four rods that hold up the canopy. Everything is clearly packaged, plastic is wrapped with very easily removable tape, several soft cushions protect from banging/scratches. Took about a two minutes to pull everything out and remove them from their bags.

Assembly: You need a phillips screwdriver and a wrench. From already having the parts out of their bags and laid out to completely done and mobile took exactly 14 minutes. It’s an extremely easy, simple, and fast assembly.
1) Pull up on the handles to unfold the wagon
2) Press down on the middle panel to snap into rigidity
3) Attach the two separated wheels, each of which is labeled L or R accordingly (the label is sort of a raised letter--black on black--you may need to look closely at the wheel strut to see it. Attaching the wheels consists of dropping the wagon atop the wheel struts, placing a washer and screw, and tightening. Simple, fast, easy.
4) attach the handle--one bolt and nut. Simple, fast, easy
5) Push the four rods into the holes for the canopy and press down
6) Attach the canopy via four snaps onto the top of the rods

The holes/snaps all lined up perfectly. There was no difficulty, no manipulation, no cursing. All as easy as could be.

To fold, simply remove the canopy and lift up the center panel. Again, worked flawlessly.

It’s a mix of plastic and fabric. But the plastic doesn’t feel cheap and the fabric seem pretty rugged. Overall build quality seems solid and as if it will last through the years with little kids.

It moves smoothly and easily. It’s very light and maneuverable. The handle is not adjustable, but it does allow you to contract it for storage. There are cup holders on either side of the inside and cup holders on the outside end at the handle.

The seats have a “seat belt”. They cannot be removed, nor do they fold flat. The canopy is a nice touch for shade and rain (though it won’t stop kids getting wet if there’s any wind slanting the rain).

Really, there’s nothing at all to complain about. If you don’t mind the price, this is an excellent and convenient pick-up
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Ultimate EZ Folding Wagon for kids and cargo, Red, Model Number: 3900

text_fidelity_a: WEQIN Water Guns for Kids Adults 1200CC Squirt Guns High 3 Nozzles Capacity Water Blaster Water Toys Summer Gun Toys Water Shooter Fighting Games Play Toys… This is a great way to cool off in the heat with the kids! My little ones loved how easy it was to replenish after using up the tank (the entire back opens up so it fills much faster), and the triple-nozzle front was a blast (literally! ha). One thing I didn't realize beforehand, however, is that it works entirely by pump action. That is, unlike a super soaker or other water pistol that builds pressure with the pump and then releases with a trigger, the pump is the entire firing mechanism, and the "trigger" is just for show (doesn't do anything). Pulling back on the pump fires the water, and the strength is adjusted  by how hard/fast you pull back. My older kids were able to figure that out, but my youngest (3 years old) found it disappointing. He likes the trigger kind because it is easy for him to fire, and with this he wasn't able to figure out the dexterity to make it shoot very far. For what it is, it works and is fun, but I do sort of wish it had a trigger that wasn't just there for looks.
text_fidelity_b: WEQIN Water Guns for Kids Adults 1200CC Squirt Guns High 3 Nozzles Capacity Water Blaster Water Toys Summer Gun Toys Water Shooter Fighting Games Play Toys…
